intro.title: List Rendering with map()
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a dynamic product catalog that displays a list of items from an array of data. You'll learn how to use Angular's structural directive *ngFor to iterate through arrays and render multiple components or elements based on your data. The core programming concept is list rendering - transforming arrays of data into visual HTML elements that users can see and interact with. You'll work with TypeScript arrays, Angular templates, and the *ngFor directive to create reusable, data-driven user interfaces. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to take any array of objects and display them as a formatted list in your Angular application.
intro.usecase: List rendering with map() is fundamental to displaying dynamic data in modern web applications. You'll use this pattern extensively when building dashboards that show arrays of user records, product listings in e-commerce sites, comment threads in social media apps, or navigation menus generated from configuration data. Every time you need to transform an array of data into a collection of UI components—whether it's displaying search results, rendering table rows, or showing a list of notifications—you'll rely on map() to iterate through the data and generate the corresponding Angular components or HTML elements.
